title: Orthogonality of Change-of-Lagrangian Intertwiners
body_html:
Orthogonality of Change-of-Lagrangian Intertwiners

Use the notation of Change-of-Lagrangian Intertwiner for Finite Schrödinger Models. Thus \(k\) has odd order \(q\), \((E,j)\) is symplectic, \(i=j/2\), and \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}:\mathcal S_{L'}\to\mathcal S_L\) is

$$ (\mathcal F_{L,L'}\varphi)(v) = \sum_{a\in L/(L\cap L')} \xi(i(a,v))\varphi(v+a). $$

Let

$$ d_{L,L'}:=\dim_k L/(L\cap L') =m-\dim_k(L\cap L'), \qquad \dim_k E=2m. $$

Statement

For all Lagrangians \(L,L'\subset E\),

$$ \mathcal F_{L,L'}\circ \mathcal F_{L',L} = q^{d_{L,L'}}\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal S_L}. $$

After interchanging \(L\) and \(L'\), also

$$ \mathcal F_{L',L}\circ \mathcal F_{L,L'} = q^{d_{L,L'}}\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal S_{L'}}. $$

Hence \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\) is an isomorphism, with inverse

$$ \mathcal F_{L,L'}^{-1}=q^{-d_{L,L'}}\mathcal F_{L',L}. $$
proof_html:
Let \(\varphi\in\mathcal S_L\). Expanding the composition gives

$$ (\mathcal F_{L,L'}\mathcal F_{L',L}\varphi)(v) = \sum_{b\in L/(L\cap L')} \xi(i(b,v)) \sum_{a\in L'/(L\cap L')} \xi(i(a,v+b))\varphi(v+b+a). $$

Because \(b\in L\), the \(L\)-covariance of \(\varphi\) gives

$$ \varphi(v+b+a) = \varphi((v+a)+b) = \xi(i(v+a,b))\varphi(v+a). $$

The total phase is

$$ i(b,v)+i(a,v+b)+i(v+a,b). $$

Expanding and using alternation of \(i\),

$$ \begin{aligned} i(b,v)+i(a,v+b)+i(v+a,b) &=i(b,v)+i(a,v)+i(a,b)+i(v,b)+i(a,b)\\ &=i(a,v)+2i(a,b)\\ &=i(a,v)+j(a,b). \end{aligned} $$

Therefore

$$ (\mathcal F_{L,L'}\mathcal F_{L',L}\varphi)(v) = \sum_{a\in L'/(L\cap L')} \xi(i(a,v))\varphi(v+a) \left(\sum_{b\in L/(L\cap L')}\xi(j(a,b))\right). $$

For fixed \(a\in L'\), the map

$$ \bar b\longmapsto \xi(j(a,b)) $$

is a character of the finite abelian group \(L/(L\cap L')\). It is trivial exactly when \(j(a,L)=0\). Since \(L\) is Lagrangian, \(L^\perp=L\); hence, for \(a\in L'\), this means \(a\in L\cap L'\).

Here is the only point using that \(\xi\) is nontrivial as an additive character of \(k\). If the \(k\)-linear functional \(b\mapsto j(a,b)\) on \(L\) is nonzero, then its image is all of \(k\). Since \(\xi\) is not trivial on \(k\), the composite \(b\mapsto \xi(j(a,b))\) is then a nontrivial character of the additive group \(L/(L\cap L')\).

Thus the inner character sum is

$$ \sum_{b\in L/(L\cap L')}\xi(j(a,b)) = \begin{cases} q^{d_{L,L'}},& a\in L\cap L',\\ 0,& a\notin L\cap L'. \end{cases} $$

The vanishing in the nontrivial case is elementary: if \(\chi\) is a nontrivial character of a finite abelian group \(A\), choose \(a_0\in A\) with \(\chi(a_0)\neq1\). For \(S=\sum_{a\in A}\chi(a)\), translation by \(a_0\) gives \(S=\chi(a_0)S\), so \((\chi(a_0)-1)S=0\). Since \(R\) is a field and \(\chi(a_0)\neq1\), one has \(S=0\).

Only the zero coset in \(L'/(L\cap L')\) survives. Hence

$$ (\mathcal F_{L,L'}\mathcal F_{L',L}\varphi)(v) =q^{d_{L,L'}}\varphi(v). $$

Repeating the same argument with \(L\) and \(L'\) interchanged gives

$$ \mathcal F_{L',L}\mathcal F_{L,L'} = q^{d_{L,L'}}\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal S_{L'}}. $$

Since \(q\) is invertible in \(R\), the displayed two-sided identities show that \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\) is invertible with the stated inverse. \(\square\)
